key_insight: Fed-ADApt lets hospitals with different compute limits jointly train segmentation models by adapting network depth during both training and inference.
clinical_relevance: This could make federated medical image segmentation more practical for under-resourced sites while preserving strong performance for tasks like retinal and brain tumor segmentation.
method: Uses multi-depth supervision in a UNet-based segmentation model.
Aggregates updates hierarchically across depth levels in federated learning.
Supports dynamic depth selection so sites can train and deploy at different compute budgets.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on multi-site 2D retinal fundus disc segmentation and 3D brain tumor segmentation, where it matched full-resource FedAvg in 3D and achieved competitive 2D results with lower inference and training cost.
watch_item: Results come from specific segmentation benchmarks, so performance and depth-selection behavior may vary across other modalities, institutions, and deployment settings.
paper_title: Fed-ADApt: Federated Anytime Depth Adaptation for Resource-Aware Medical Image Segmentation
